### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**25** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3837bf7ffbe49e1c11df6ba421a61c2d621e4188` — the merge of head `506782945fd54b00d5ea4e4f8717d1049c23d03c` into base `c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3837bf7ffbe49e1c11df6ba421a61c2d621e4188 && git checkout 3837bf7ffbe49e1c11df6ba421a61c2d621e4188
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d 506782945fd54b00d5ea4e4f8717d1049c23d03c && git checkout -B drift-repro c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d && git merge --no-ff 506782945fd54b00d5ea4e4f8717d1049c23d03c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c4196099eee97f9fc48995063dde978fe5516a5d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3e09f3499f39756036d4774816589bed4ee2333`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/32768-upload-link-readonly-when-at-issue.md, packages/objectql/src/engine-field-write-lock.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-field-write-lock.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/readonly-strict-errors.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.integration.test.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts, content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx + packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/file-attachment-service.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts (cited code outside the diff, read, not reviewed)

Read at 2026-11-13T09:44Z: the diff against merge base `4079b06b`, the live PR body, card #32768 with claim 6847540308, re-post 6847846915 and report 6849438419, and the head's check-runs. Narrowing face (no schema or governed path in the tree; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on body and changeset).

### ① Derived judgments

- Check-runs on the head at read time: 16 completed success (among them Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Lint · docs & code guards); 19 still in progress (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, five Lint families, Live E2E UI); none failed. This record does not stand in for the pending ones.
- The dogfood shards do not run on `pull_request` by workflow design, so the dogfood pin's evidence is the dev's local battery at `d9c65672` (458 files, 3845 tests, exit 0). The one later commit touches only the objectql unit-test driver double; read in the diff, true.
- Report claims read against the code: no `packages/spec` path and no `engine-validate.ts` in the diff (true); `file-content.ts` untouched (true); the surface correction to `service-storage` is declared on re-post 6847846915 before the push (true).
- Ablation (report): removing the refusal line in `record-file-access.ts` fails exactly the new integration pin. The pin's shape agrees: it asserts code, status, the whole sentence and an unchanged open-link row count, all of which need the refusal.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/mcp`: correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` is true (no key, value or metadata type moves), and a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its banner. The three packages are exactly the published ones the diff moves; the dogfood package and docs publish nothing.
- BREAKING banner present on the changeset and the PR body, with FROM, TO and the one-line fix; `fix(...)!:` title agrees.
- ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is present and its reason holds: no schema key or stored shape moves. Check Changeset, which runs the registration check, is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: correct arm. The tool issues less than it did. The accompanying widening (one public method `ObjectQL#judgeFieldWriteLock`, one type export `FieldWriteLock` from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) is declared in the changeset prose and the claim's declaration note; one arm per line, and narrowing is the governing one.
- `readonlyDropReasonPhrase` is exported from its module only, not from the package entry; true of `index.ts`.
- `IDataEngine` (spec) is not widened: `service-storage` reads the method as an optional member of its own `RecordFileEngine` interface. An engine without it is not asked and the consume-side strict write still refuses.
- `engine.validate` / `ValidateDataResponse`: not in the diff; the documented limit ("`readonlyWhen` is not run") does not move.
- `Skills-docs: none` holds: nothing under `skills/**` names `create_upload_link`. The tool description and `connect-mcp.mdx` carry the refusal.

### ④ Design judgment

- The judgement is the engine's own evaluation. `judgeFieldWriteLock` calls `stripReadonlyWhenFields` (the function `engine-update.ts` calls for the by-id update), with `previous` from `readUpdatePriorRow` and `parent` from `resolveMasterDetailParent` behind `hasParentScopedReadonlyWhenInPayload`, the update's own gate. No CEL is evaluated in `service-storage` or `packages/mcp`. With the payload carrying the stored value, `record` equals the stored row, so any predicate over other fields gets the verdict the upload's write gets. The two places it can differ from the write (`beforeUpdate` hooks not run; a predicate reading the incoming value of its own field) are named on the method. In both the consume-side strict write still judges, so the worst case is a link whose upload is refused (the old behaviour) or a refusal slightly early; never an attach past a lock.
- The narrowing makes an existing refusal real earlier; it takes no working capability away. FROM and TO are true of the code: before, the link was minted and the PUT answered `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` "Nothing was attached: ..."; now `createUploadLinkAs` refuses before `store.createFile`, so no link row is written.
- Complete over the doors: `createUploadLinkAs` has one implementation (`RecordFileAccess`), one delegate (`FileAttachmentService`) and one caller (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, the MCP bridge). The REST routes under `/storage/upload-links/:token` only open and spend a link; no REST or SDK door mints one. The attachments target takes the `field === undefined` branch and is not judged; pinned by the integration test.
- Code and words: `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, the code this door already answers for static `readonly` and for the same lock at consume time. The phrase is `REASON_PHRASE.readonly_when` read through the new accessor, not re-spelled. The dogfood pin ties it to the lock `update_record` reports on the same field (`droppedFields`, reason `readonly_when`).
- should-fix (docs wording, `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`): "the words `update_record`'s strict refusal uses". MCP `update_record` has no strict mode; it reports the lock under `droppedFields` with reason `readonly_when`. The words are the engine update's strict refusal (`strictReadonlyWrites`). Say that, or name the `droppedFields` reason.
- nit: for the same lock the door now speaks two sentences, the engine phrase at issue and "read-only on this record in its current state" at consume. Both true; the reader differs (agent, then person).
- nit: a record that is both `readonlyWhen`-locked and approval-locked now answers 403 where it answered `409 RECORD_LOCKED`. Refused either way.
- nit: `UPLOAD_LINK_TOOL_LINES` in `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` names no field refusal; it named none before, so nothing regresses.

No must-fix.
